body.en: Trigonometry and Additional Topics comprise approximately 5% of the EST I Mathematics exam (primarily appearing in Section II). Key competencies include evaluating trigonometric ratios using SOH-CAH-TOA, exploiting the complementary cofunction identity $\sin(x) = \cos(90^\circ - x)$, applying radian-degree conversions ($180^\circ = \pi\text{ rad}$), simplifying expressions using the Pythagorean identity $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$, and performing complex number arithmetic ($i^2 = -1$).

label.en: Definition 7.1 — Trigonometric Ratios, Radians, and the Complex Number System

body.en:
Core definitions of trigonometric ratios and complex numbers:
  • Right-Triangle Trigonometric Ratios (SOH-CAH-TOA):
    For acute angle \(\theta\) in a right triangle:
    \[ \sin\theta = \frac{\text{Opposite}}{\text{Hypotenuse}}, \qquad \cos\theta = \frac{\text{Adjacent}}{\text{Hypotenuse}}, \qquad \tan\theta = \frac{\text{Opposite}}{\text{Adjacent}} \]
  • Reciprocal Trigonometric Ratios:
    \[ \csc\theta = \frac{1}{\sin\theta} = \frac{\text{Hyp}}{\text{Opp}}, \qquad \sec\theta = \frac{1}{\cos\theta} = \frac{\text{Hyp}}{\text{Adj}}, \qquad \cot\theta = \frac{1}{\tan\theta} = \frac{\text{Adj}}{\text{Opp}} \]
  • Radian Measure: One radian is the measure of a central angle that intercepts an arc equal in length to the circle's radius. The conversion equivalence is:
    \[ \pi\text{ radians} = 180^\circ \implies 1\text{ rad} = \frac{180^\circ}{\pi}, \quad 1^\circ = \frac{\pi}{180^\circ}\text{ rad} \]
  • Complex Number System (\(\mathbb{C}\)):
    A complex number has standard form \(z = a + bi\), where \(a, b \in \mathbb{R}\) and \(i = \sqrt{-1}\) such that \(i^2 = -1\).
    1. Powers of \(i\) (Cyclic modulo 4): \(i^1 = i\), \(i^2 = -1\), \(i^3 = -i\), \(i^4 = 1\).
    2. Complex Conjugate: \(\bar{z} = a - bi\), with real product \(z \bar{z} = a^2 + b^2\).
    3. Modulus: \(|z| = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\).

label.en: ● Deep Conceptual Intuition — Trigonometry & Additional Topics

body.en: Unit Circle Periodicity, Harmonic Synthesis & Triangle Laws: Every angle \(\theta\) on the unit circle defines \((\cos\theta, \sin\theta)\) with fundamental Pythagorean invariance \(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta \equiv 1\). Linear combinations of同-frequency waves \(a\cos\theta \pm b\sin\theta\) collapse into a single phase-shifted sinusoid \(R\cos(\theta \mp \alpha)\) where \(R = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\) and \(\tan\alpha = b/a\), immediately revealing the exact maximum \(+R\) and minimum \(-R\).

label.en: Theorem 7.1 — Cofunction Complementarity, Pythagorean Identities, and Complex Division

body.en:
Fundamental identities and algebraic procedures:
  • Complementary Angle Theorem (Cofunction Identity):
    In any right triangle with acute angles \(A\) and \(B\) such that \(A + B = 90^\circ\) (or \(\frac{\pi}{2}\text{ rad}\)):
    \[ \sin A = \cos(90^\circ - A) = \cos B \]
    \[ \cos A = \sin(90^\circ - A) = \sin B \]
    \[ \tan A = \cot(90^\circ - A) = \frac{1}{\tan B} \]
  • Pythagorean Trigonometric Identities:
    1. \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\)
    2. \(1 + \tan^2\theta = \sec^2\theta\)
    3. \(1 + \cot^2\theta = \csc^2\theta\)
  • Special Right Triangle Values (Unit Circle):
    1. \(30^\circ = \frac{\pi}{6}\): \(\sin 30^\circ = \frac{1}{2}\), \(\cos 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), \(\tan 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\).
    2. \(45^\circ = \frac{\pi}{4}\): \(\sin 45^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\), \(\cos 45^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\), \(\tan 45^\circ = 1\).
    3. \(60^\circ = \frac{\pi}{3}\): \(\sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), \(\cos 60^\circ = \frac{1}{2}\), \(\tan 60^\circ = \sqrt{3}\).
  • Division of Complex Numbers: Multiply numerator and denominator by the complex conjugate of the denominator to eliminate \(i\) from the denominator:
    \[ \frac{a + bi}{c + di} = \frac{(a + bi)(c - di)}{(c + di)(c - di)} = \frac{(ac + bd) + (bc - ad)i}{c^2 + d^2} \]

label.en: ▲ EST I Math Traps & Pitfalls — Trigonometry & Additional Topics

body.en:
• Radian vs. Degree Mode: If evaluating trigonometric ratios on a calculator, always verify your active mode! Evaluating \(\sin(30)\) in radian mode yields \(-0.988\) instead of \(0.5\).
  • Complementary Angle Theorem: In any right triangle, the acute angles sum to \(90^\circ\), which implies \(\sin(x) = \cos(90^\circ - x)\) and \(\cos(x) = \sin(90^\circ - x)\). If \(\sin(A) = \cos(B)\), then \(A + B = 90^\circ\).
  • Pythagorean Identity Variations: \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\) rearranges to \(\sin^2\theta = 1 - \cos^2\theta = (1 - \cos\theta)(1 + \cos\theta)\). Recognizing this difference of squares simplifies many algebraic trig questions instantly.
  • Powers of \(i\) Cyclicity: Powers of the imaginary unit cycle every 4 powers: \(i^1 = i\), \(i^2 = -1\), \(i^3 = -i\), \(i^4 = 1\). To evaluate \(i^n\), divide \(n\) by 4 and use the remainder.
  • Complex Multiplication Errors: Remember that \(i^2 = -1\), so \((a + bi)^2 = a^2 + 2abi + b^2 i^2 = (a^2 - b^2) + 2abi\). Do NOT write \(a^2 + b^2\) for the square of a binomial!

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Trigonometry & Additional Topics)

body.en:
Why the Harmonic \(R\)-Formula & Cosine Rule Hold: Expanding \(R\cos(\theta - \alpha)\) via the compound-angle identity gives:

\[ R\cos(\theta - \alpha) = (R\cos\alpha)\cos\theta + (R\sin\alpha)\sin\theta \]

Matching coefficients with \(a\cos\theta + b\sin\theta\) requires \(R\cos\alpha = a\) and \(R\sin\alpha = b\). Squaring and adding yields \(R^2(\cos^2\alpha + \sin^2\alpha) = a^2 + b^2 \implies R = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\), and dividing gives \(\tan\alpha = \dfrac{b}{a}\).

label.en: Worked Example 7.A — Cofunction Equalities & Angle Algebra

body.en:
In a right triangle with acute angles \(A\) and \(B\), it is given that \(\sin(4x - 10^\circ) = \cos(3x + 16^\circ)\).
(a) Find the value of \(x\).
(b) Determine the exact value of \(\sin(x + 18^\circ)\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. (a) Use the Cofunction Complementarity Theorem:
    Since \(\sin(u) = \cos(v)\) for acute angles, the two angles are complementary: \[ u + v = 90^\circ \]
    Substitute the expressions:
    \[ (4x - 10^\circ) + (3x + 16^\circ) = 90^\circ \implies 7x + 6^\circ = 90^\circ \implies 7x = 84^\circ \implies \mathbf{x = 12^\circ} \]
  2. (b) Evaluate \(\sin(x + 18^\circ)\):
    Substitute \(x = 12^\circ\):
    \[ \sin(12^\circ + 18^\circ) = \sin(30^\circ) = \mathbf{\frac{1}{2} = 0.5} \]

Simplify the expression \(\dfrac{1 - \cos^2\theta}{\sin\theta \cos\theta}\) and express it in terms of a single fundamental trigonometric function.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Recall the Pythagorean identity: \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1 \implies 1 - \cos^2\theta = \sin^2\theta\).
  2. Substitute \(\sin^2\theta\) into the numerator:
    \[ \frac{1 - \cos^2\theta}{\sin\theta \cos\theta} = \frac{\sin^2\theta}{\sin\theta \cos\theta} \]
  3. Cancel one factor of \(\sin\theta\) from numerator and denominator:
    \[ \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \mathbf{\tan\theta} \]
The simplified expression is \(\mathbf{\tan\theta}\).

label.en: Worked Example 7.C — Complex Number Operations & Rationalization

body.en:
(a) Express the quotient \(\dfrac{7 + 4i}{2 - 3i}\) in standard complex form \(a + bi\).
(b) Evaluate the sum of powers \(i^{2024} + i^{2025} + i^{2026} + i^{2027}\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. (a) Multiply by the conjugate \(2 + 3i\):
    \[ \frac{7 + 4i}{2 - 3i} = \frac{(7 + 4i)(2 + 3i)}{(2 - 3i)(2 + 3i)} \]
    Expand denominator: \(2^2 - (3i)^2 = 4 - 9(-1) = 4 + 9 = 13\).
    Expand numerator using FOIL:
    \[ (7)(2) + 21i + 8i + 12i^2 = 14 + 29i + 12(-1) = (14 - 12) + 29i = 2 + 29i \]
    Divide both parts by 13:
    \[ \mathbf{\frac{2}{13} + \frac{29}{13}i} \]
  2. (b) Evaluate sum of powers of \(i\):
    Any four consecutive integer powers of \(i\) sum to 0:
    Since \(2024 = 4 \times 506\) (remainder 0): \(i^{2024} = 1\).
    \(i^{2025} = i\), \(i^{2026} = -1\), \(i^{2027} = -i\).
    \[ 1 + i - 1 - i = \mathbf{0} \]

label.en: Worked Example \(D\) — Trigonometry & Additional Topics (Easy Application)

body.en:
Problem (Easy): Point \( C \) has polar coordinates \( (r, \theta) = (20, 60^\circ) \) in the plane. What is its Cartesian coordinate \( p = r\cos\theta \)?

Step-by-Step Solution: Using \( p = 20\cos(60^\circ) = 20 \times \frac{1}{2} = 10 \).

body.en: All-Solutions Checklist (Egyptian Scholastic Test (EST I — Literacy & Math)): When solving \(\trig(kx + \phi) = c\) on \([0, 2\pi]\), immediately write down the transformed interval \(\phi \le u \le 2k\pi + \phi\), list all ASTC quadrant angles in that range, and only divide by \(k\) at the very last step.

question.en: In a right triangle, acute angle \(\theta\) satisfies \(\sin\theta = \dfrac{5}{13}\). Find the exact values of \(\cos\theta\), \(\tan\theta\), and \(\sec\theta\).

solution.en:
Step 1: In a right triangle with opposite side \(5\) and hypotenuse \(13\), the adjacent side is: \[ \text{adj} = \sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = \sqrt{169 - 25} = \sqrt{144} = 12. \]

Step 2: Compute trigonometric ratios:

  • \(\cos\theta = \dfrac{\text{adj}}{\text{hyp}} = \mathbf{\dfrac{12}{13}}\).
  • \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}} = \mathbf{\dfrac{5}{12}}\).
  • \(\sec\theta = \dfrac{1}{\cos\theta} = \mathbf{\dfrac{13}{12}}\).

Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \(5\).

question.en: If \(\cos(2x + 10^\circ) = \sin(3x - 15^\circ)\), find the value of \(x\) and evaluate \(\tan(x + 16^\circ)\).

solution.en:
Step 1: Apply cofunction identity \(\cos A = \sin B \iff A + B = 90^\circ\): \[ (2x + 10^\circ) + (3x - 15^\circ) = 90^\circ \implies 5x - 5^\circ = 90^\circ \implies 5x = 95^\circ \implies \mathbf{x = 19^\circ}. \]

Step 2: Evaluate tangent: \[ \tan(19^\circ + 16^\circ) = \tan(35^\circ) \approx \mathbf{0.7002}. \]

Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \(\cos A = \sin B \iff A + B = 90^\circ\).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

question.en: Convert \(\dfrac{7\pi}{6}\) radians to degrees, and find the exact coordinates of its terminal point on the unit circle.

solution.en:
Step 1: Convert to degrees: \[ \theta = \frac{7\pi}{6} \times \frac{180^\circ}{\pi} = 7 \times 30^\circ = \mathbf{210^\circ}. \]

Step 2: Terminal coordinates in Quadrant III: The reference angle is \(210^\circ - 180^\circ = 30^\circ\). In Quadrant III, both coordinates are negative: \[ x = \cos(210^\circ) = -\cos(30^\circ) = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}, \qquad y = \sin(210^\circ) = -\sin(30^\circ) = -\frac{1}{2}. \]

The terminal point is \(\mathbf{\left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}, -\frac{1}{2}\right)}\).

question.en: Evaluate the complex expression \(\dfrac{(3 - 2i)^2}{1 + i}\) and write the result in standard form \(a + bi\).

solution.en:
Step 1: Expand the numerator: \[ (3 - 2i)^2 = 3^2 - 2(3)(2i) + (2i)^2 = 9 - 12i + 4(-1) = 5 - 12i. \]

Step 2: Multiply by conjugate \(1 - i\): \[ \frac{5 - 12i}{1 + i} = \frac{(5 - 12i)(1 - i)}{(1 + i)(1 - i)} = \frac{5 - 5i - 12i + 12i^2}{1 - i^2} = \frac{5 - 17i - 12}{1 - (-1)} = \frac{-7 - 17i}{2}. \]

In standard form: \(\mathbf{-\frac{7}{2} - \frac{17}{2}i}\).

Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \( (3 - 2i)^2 = 3^2 - 2(3)(2i) + (2i)^2 = 9 - 12i + 4(-1) = 5 - 12i. \).
